comment: Frame 038, printed p. 32: the cities of the sixth clime continued, entries 459-474: ماطنڡا and روران at the mountain, جزان, Sīsajān, Nashwā, a city at the mountain between the two gates, Bardhaʿa, Rafsā at the mountain and the gate of the Khazar, Khwārizm, al-Khazar, Nawākath, two entries that are the word «مدينة» alone, Dirsāq, the city of Yājūj and the city of Mājūj; the folio of the manuscript, «(fol. 8ᵇ)», in the margin. Three lines of the editor's footnotes.

variants: L01: the manuscript has a gap in the coordinates; the editor supplies them from S.
L03: the manuscript reads حرران, without dots; at entry (2120) the name is written جزران, with the variant reading جرجان.
L07: the manuscript reads ٮرذعه, without the dot of the ب and with a final ه; at entry (2120) the name is written ٮردعه, without dots.
L08: at entry (2120) the name is written باسيا.
L11: the manuscript reads ٮواكث, without the dot of the ن.
observations: The table goes on from frame 037 without a heading: the cities of the sixth clime, entries 459-474. Entry 474 has no number of Suhrāb; the others have [٤١٩], [٤٢١], [٤٢٠], [٤٢٢], [٤٢٣], [٤٢٦], [٣٩٠], [٤٢٥] (entries 459-466) and [٤٢٧]-[٤٣٣] (entries 467-473); [٤٢٤] stands at entry 444 (frame 036). Entries 464, 473 and 474 begin with the word «مدينة»; entries 470 and 471 are the word alone. The folio of the Strasbourg manuscript, «(fol. 8ᵇ)», is printed in Latin type in the right margin beside entry 460 (L02).

L01: the coordinates of entry 459 are printed «س⟨ح ك⟩» and «⟨مٮ ل⟩», each followed by the note mark a: the editor supplies the second letter of the degrees and the minutes of the longitude, and the whole latitude, from S, where the manuscript has a gap (note a). The opening bracket of the longitude stands between the س and the ح of the degrees, the س outside it. Transcribed with the brackets where they stand.
L01: «ماطنڡا»: after «ما», a ط, a low tooth with a dot above it, the ن, and a loop without dots joined to the final alif; transcribed ماطنڡا.
L05: «نشوى» ends in a ى without dots.

Letters printed without their dots in the numerals, transcribed so: مٮ (L01, L09, L13, L14, the degrees of the latitude), the م and a final ب without its dot, 42; عٮ (L06, the degrees of the longitude), 72; the loop of ف or ق without dots in the degrees of the longitude, ڡد (L11), ڡى (L12), ڡٮ (L13, the ب without its dot), ڡا (L14), ڡع (L15) and ڡعا (L16), the loop joined to a medial ع and a final alif. With their dots: عج (L08) and مج (L15), the ج with its dot in the bowl; ن (L06, the minutes of the latitude; L08, L09, the minutes of the longitude).

The degrees printed with a final ح, the ح of «س⟨ح» (L01), عح (L07) and صح (L10), and مح (L07, the degrees of the latitude), show no dot in the bowl; the same form is a ج without its dot, 3, which the print gives with its dot in عج (L08) and مج (L15). Transcribed as printed.
The isolated ك, 20, is printed with the small inner stroke of the letter (L01, the minutes of the longitude).

Specks, not transcribed: L06, a speck between the minutes and the degrees of the longitude; L12, two faint specks above the degrees of the longitude, «ڡى»; L14, a speck, 4 by 4 px, beside the foot of the ل of the minutes of the longitude, where the dots of the font are some 9 px across.
The page number «— ٣٢ —» stands at the foot, centred.
copy_matter: Faint wavy grey hairlines, fibres on the paper: L07, between the columns of the latitude; L08, below «الجبل».
